package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS gateways since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because a developer surreptitiously inserted JavaScript code into the Tornado Cash user interface that exfiltrates users’ private deposit notes (which function as private keys) to an external server, enabling theft of user funds. This code was hidden within a governance proposal and affected all users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.file_location: Tornado Cash UI JavaScript source (injected via governance proposal, deployed to IPFS gateways)
required_permissions: access to in-memory deposit notes (private keys)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the code accesses the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, enabling credential exfiltration and potential fund theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it covertly exfiltrates sensitive user secrets (deposit notes/private keys) to an external server without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or keys off-device or to any third party. The actual behavior directly violates user privacy and security by leaking secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or error reporting might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private keys or deposit notes.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive in-memory secrets (deposit notes)
Encoding and network transmission of secrets to hardcoded external domain
No user notification or consent for this data transfer
Code hidden within a governance proposal (supply chain attack vector)

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive governance proposal and deployed to IPFS gateways.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious code in users' browsers when they interact with the UI.

attack_chain.action: When a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the malicious code captures the user's private deposit note.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of the deposit note to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: The encoded deposit note is sent via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains the ability to access and steal user funds.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs that accesses deposit notes or private keys and sends them to external domains
Network requests from the UI to non-official, hardcoded domains during sensitive user actions
Obfuscated or hidden code introduced via governance or community proposals
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in Tornado Cash UI JavaScript files deployed to IPFS
Functions that serialize and transmit deposit notes or private keys
References to external domains not associated with Tornado Cash
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from the UI to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., https://attacker-server.com/collect)
Outbound traffic containing encoded deposit notes or similar secrets
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DeFi UI codebases for any code that accesses and transmits deposit notes, private keys, or other secrets to external domains. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag JavaScript that performs network requests with sensitive data. Watch for unauthorized changes in open-source repositories, especially those introduced via governance proposals. On the network side, alert on POST requests from user browsers to non-official domains during DeFi interactions.
